name: Biztha
overview: Biztha was a male eunuch who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus. He is identified as one of the seven eunuchs holding this position, as recorded in the book of Esther. Scripture provides no additional tribal or familial details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Biztha possibly means 'eunuch' or 'bound,' reflecting his status or role. This name is recorded in Esther 1:10 and does not appear to have been given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Biztha beyond his role as one of the seven eunuchs serving King Ahasuerus.
scriptureSignificance: Biztha's significance lies in his service to King Ahasuerus, marking him as part of the royal court's inner circle. As one of the seven eunuchs, he would have had responsibilities related to the king's immediate presence, contributing to the administration and security of the palace. His mention in Esther 1:10 places him within the historical context of the Persian empire's governance.
